correspondence.finding: The selected northeastern opening and successive southwest-going parts coincide with the directly labelled Unuk River channel and its locally broad water-filled corridor in Canada. The opening begins within this continuing river; the map does not establish it as a natural headwater. All four original parts remain distinct in the review.

The selection continues southwest through the connected Unuk channel, narrows between broader reaches, then turns west along the final Canadian approach to the border. Side creeks join the same mapped trunk; they are not substituted for the selected river. Although Canadian relief detail is sparse in this composite, the drawn channel connections and repeated Unuk labels are explicit.

This original part carries the selected Unuk corridor across the mapped Canada–United States boundary into southeastern Alaska. The river continues directly through the boundary without a geographic break. The country transition lies within this part; a surveyed crossing position or name-change boundary is not asserted.

The route turns southwest and then south through the wide mapped Unuk alluvial/braided floor between mountain slopes. The simplified selection stays within that one connected river corridor. Modern braid positions, exact banks and every small intervening bar are outside the supported scale.

correspondence.component_scope: blue river junction and fragment end
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor resumes southwest and approaches the Blue River tributary junction. The source map labels the continuing receiving trunk Unuk River; the tributary from the north remains separately identified. The final part reaches the retained fragment boundary along the same continuous river floor.

The next stored fragment begins at the preceding fragment ending and follows the southwest-going Unuk continuation below the northern tributary approach. All four short original parts cross the connected channel/alluvial corridor, without inserting an artificial break at the stage or fragment boundary.

The selected course turns south and southwest through a broad, repeatedly labelled Unuk braided valley. The river floor remains continuous across all five original parts and between steep valley margins; separate modern threads are not required to coincide with the generalized line.

The river bends west and then southwest along the widening lower Unuk valley. The mapped trunk, side channels and downstream alluvial floor form a continuous receiving corridor approaching the coastal delta. The separately labelled Luke Creek approach is lateral tributary context, not the selected trunk.

The last original part crosses the broad lower delta and turns northwest near its end. The source ending is in the channel-and-island delta setting, while the rendered ending lies slightly farther north within the adjoining distributary/interdistributary delta floor. Both are separately located in the original map. Their ordinary shared delta connection is supported, but the final generalized segment is not equated with one exact mapped wet thread, bank, seaward mouth or shoreline.

correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening and westward valley route follow the directly labelled Sitkum River, including its southwest bend and downstream return west. The initial point is within the mapped river rather than its demonstrated natural source. All five original parts remain in the same connected valley between the surrounding ridges.

This short part reaches the common valley junction where the selected Sitkum approach joins the South Fork Calawah corridor arriving from the southeast. The mapped blue channels are connected. Exact legal name limits or a surveyed confluence point are not inferred from the simplified selection.

The selection turns northwest and west along the labelled South Fork Calawah River, then passes the North Fork approach and the transition into the Calawah trunk. The main channel and valley floor remain connected across all five original parts. The local source scale supports the fork sequence without assigning an exact part-vertex name boundary.

The route continues west and southwest on the directly labelled Calawah River beside the Forks setting, then reaches its junction with the Bogachiel River. Local meanders differ from the generalized line but occupy the same continuous alluvial floor. The stage-3 fragment remains unchanged.

The selected receiving route runs southwest and west through the directly labelled lower Bogachiel corridor, crossing the broad floodplain and road setting before its junction with the Sol Duc River. The Sol Duc is a distinct northern tributary, not a substitute for the selected upstream route. All four original parts have connected valley/channel support.

Below the Bogachiel–Sol Duc junction, the selection follows the broad westward river directly labelled Quillayute River. It continues toward the Dickey River approach and the coastal mouth beside the Quileute Reservation. Quillayute is the named final receiver and representative candidate; the upper component names remain distinct.

The separate stage-2 terminal fragment continues west from the prior fragment into the mapped Quillayute mouth/coastal opening. Its source ending lies at the mouth-side coastal transition, and its rendered ending lies slightly farther southwest toward open coastal water. Both definitions were inspected separately. The generalized terminal line is supported at mouth-setting scale without claiming a precise contemporary bank, tidal channel or shoreline.

Separate orientation aids located every part and both ending definitions. correspondence.finding: The chosen northern opening runs south through the wooded lowland drainage depicted on the atlas as the headward part of the Kung Kung corridor. The photograph shows the same low-relief drainage setting, with canopy and small clouds limiting wet-thread visibility. The atlas supplies the continuous mapped through-link. This is a selected interior opening, not a verified natural source.

The route turns east and then southeast along the continuous northern feeder. Both original atlas maps directly label this corridor Kung Kung and distinguish it from the Río Grande de Matagalpa drainage farther north. The photographic vegetation/drainage strip and local channel portions follow the same ordinary corridor.

The selected northern feeder turns south through low wetland ground and reaches the common Kurinwas junction. Its final part meets both the stored western tributary terminal and the beginning of FID10675. Atlas river linework establishes the through-link; the imagery shows the surrounding connected lowland and adjoining open river. The feeder name is not extended downstream past the receiving junction.

From the common junction the selection follows the eastward receiving river, including the northerly bend and return toward the coastal wetlands. The atlas directly labels the downstream course Kurinwas. The photograph shows a broad, winding river in the same alluvial corridor.

The receiving river continues east among adjacent wetland lakes, then turns south toward the northern Laguna de Perlas entry. Both atlas cartography and the photograph preserve the connected channel between the lateral waterbodies. The generalized selection is not required to reproduce every modern meander. Names are not assigned to the lateral lakes from proximity alone.

The final mainstem part follows the southern turn at the river mouth and extends east into the northern receiving lagoon. The source-endpoint metadata locates the river-mouth/lagoon-entry margin; the rendered endpoint lies farther east in lagoon water. They are treated separately. The atlas explicitly identifies the receiving water as Laguna de Perlas, and Incer independently says Kurinwás empties into that lagoon. The inventory terminal class is sea, but the selected endpoint is not the Caribbean ocean outlet. No downstream traverse to the lagoon’s ocean connection is part of this selection.

This stored tributary starts farther west in a wooded, low-relief drainage and runs generally east, with a southern bend and intervening joins, toward the broader western Kurinwas corridor. The original atlas network and the visible wooded/channel corridor supply the connected sequence. The chosen western opening and its initial feeder are not independently named here; the representative Kurinwas name is not imposed on every upstream part. The grouping boundary is an observation interval, not a surveyed legal name-transition point.

The remaining stage3 tributary parts continue east in the mapped western Kurinwas drainage north of El Tortuguero, with repeated bends and lateral tributary joins. The atlas directly labels the western receiving course on the complementary Río Grande de Matagalpa regional map and depicts it continuously on the RAAS map. The photograph shows the corresponding wooded alluvial corridor and widening visible river toward the eastern fragment join. The inventory role remains tributary even though it follows part of the geographically named Kurinwas course.

The stage2 tributary continues from the preceding fragment through the same eastgoing Kurinwas floodplain, with a northern sweep followed by a southeastward bend. Visible river meanders in the photographic original and the continuous atlas linework support all nine parts at ordinary corridor scale.

These parts follow the lower western Kurinwas course through its broad southern meandering bend. The simplified line locally cuts across individual loops while remaining within the same connected alluvial floor. The atlas and imagery support the valley/corridor connection; no present channel-bank or perennial-flow assertion is made.

The last four tributary parts turn northeast and reach the common junction with the northern Kung Kung feeder and FID10675. The tributary source and render endpoints coincide in the same confluence setting. This is the aggregate geometry’s final coordinate because the tributary is stored last; it is not the mainstem terminal. All original role and order information is preserved.

No reordering, reversal, joining, simplification or geometry repair was performed.

findings.completion_scope: All74 original parts across all five actual inventory components were compared with freshly read retained atlas originals and one completed photographic view with overlapping unmarked crops. The selected openings, mainstem and tributary joins, complete western/northern corridors, lower receiving river and separate source/render lagoon-entry positions have ordinary connected-geography support. No necessary receiver or through-link remains materially unresolved.

correspondence.finding: The opening occupies a snow/ice-margin and rocky headward depression, then descends east-southeast beside a small glacial waterbody into the forested drainage valley. The imagery supports the ordinary headward corridor without locating a surveyed source or present ice-front position.

The selection continues east through the same broad valley and alluvial floor, then turns south near a pale sediment-bearing waterbody. Multiple small channels, the open floor and enclosing slopes support ordinary corridor continuity; no name is assigned to the upper waterbodies.

The southward reach follows a broad wetland and channel-bearing lowland to the northern approach of the large upper lake. The continuous valley floor is visible despite the lack of a single uniformly resolved wet thread.

The route enters the large green-toned upper lake, follows its western-to-southern bend and then its eastward arm. Generalized edge offsets stay in this lake/shore corridor. The upper lake is kept distinct from Lago Muñoz Gamero and receives no assigned name.

After the eastern upper-lake arm, the selected part turns northeast across a sustained wooded and locally knobby land interval toward the northern inlet of the lower lake. The detailed image does not establish a continuous low through-valley or watercourse along this crossing. A different outlet-like low corridor is visible farther southeast, but it is not proof of the selected connection. Shipton describes carrying a boat between the named lower lake and the unnamed upper lake; that travel account does not establish a water connection.

The route reaches the northern inlet and continues south through the long lower-lake arm. This is the lower-lake side of the unresolved preceding link. Its broad water corridor is supported independently of whether the modeled interlake crossing is valid.

All nine original parts occupy the long north-south lower-lake corridor, mostly close to its western side. Side arms remain distinct. The image mosaic and minor shoreline offsets do not create a separate necessary connection gap.

The selection continues south and slightly east through the lower-lake basin to its constricted southern turn. Both sides of the narrowing and its continuity into the next original fragment are visible; the stage boundary is preserved.

The next fragment follows the narrowing southwest into a wider lower-lake basin. The full original water corridor is continuous through the retained stage2 parts, including the long southwest diagonal.

The route follows the southwestern lake finger toward its outlet approach. Water, the enclosing low shore and the outgoing valley are visible; this is bounded Lago Muñoz Gamero/outflow context, not a representative river-name assignment.

The last two parts leave the southwestern lake finger through the short low outlet corridor to the sediment-plume/coastal receiving-water setting. The source endpoint and the slightly northwest render endpoint were separately located; the overview does not resolve their small offset against an exact current mouth or shoreline. Their shared outlet-to-coastal corridor is supported, and neither endpoint definition is replaced.

FID 14671 has local parts 0–31, identical to aggregate parts 0–31; FID 14672 has local parts 0–11, aggregate 32–43. These are one-based local parts 1–32 and 1–12 respectively. All 44 original parts, 129 positions, two mainstem roles, fragment order and stages 3/2 remain unchanged; no joining, reversal, simplification or repair. Source and render endings remain separate.
